# Permission matrix

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask matrix` from `crates/testkit/matrix/expectations.toml`. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the permission oracle of Davhaven in readable form: what every actor gets when it does every operation on every kind of calendar through every surface, and when it calls every administration operation of the management API. The permission matrix of the test suite sends each of these cases to the real application, in process on the memory and PostgreSQL stores, and fails when an answer differs from the table; it also checks that a refusal changes nothing (no sequence bump, no outbox item, no event) and that its body does not leak what the caller may not see. The cases that must change nothing run against a deployed instance as well (`davhaven-conformance run`). The oracle is written by hand and reviewed against the authorization rules in the management API and protocol documentation; it is never computed from the authorization code it checks.

## Status policy

| Code | Expectation | HTTP | Challenge | DAV precondition | Problem code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `A` | allow | 2xx |  |  |  | the operation succeeds (200, 201, 204, 207 ...) |
| `U` | unauthenticated | 401 | `WWW-Authenticate` |  | `unauthenticated` | no or invalid credentials, a suspended principal or tenant, or a credential presented on a surface it is not bound to; the response carries WWW-Authenticate (Basic on dav, Bearer on api and mcp) |
| `H` | hidden | 404 |  |  | `not-found` | no read visibility, including other tenants' and unknown resources; indistinguishable from a missing resource |
| `F` | forbidden | 403 |  | `DAV:need-privileges` | `forbidden` | visible but not permitted: DAV answers with DAV:need-privileges, the API and MCP with the problem `forbidden` |
| `P` | precondition_failed | 412 |  |  | `precondition-failed` | a stale If-Match or If-Schedule-Tag-Match; not an authorization decision, listed for the precondition cases |

A `*` after a code marks a case that an exception row of the expectations file decides; the default rules (effective access against what the operation needs) decide all the others.

## Actors

| Actor | Tenant | Principal | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | acme | `olivia` | Owns the personal, the shared and the mirror calendar. |
| `group_member` | acme | `mia` | Member of the group `team` (owner of the group calendar) and, through it, a reader of the managed calendar. |
| `sharee_read` | acme | `rita` | Accepted a read share of the shared calendar. |
| `sharee_read_write` | acme | `wanda` | Accepted a read-write share of the shared calendar. |
| `grantee_via_group` | acme | `gary` | Reads the shared calendar through a grant to the group `viewers`. |
| `pending_sharee` | acme | `paul` | Was invited to the shared calendar and has not answered. |
| `declined_sharee` | acme | `dora` | Declined the invitation to the shared calendar. |
| `other_user` | acme | `otto` | A user of the tenant without access to anything of the others. |
| `other_tenant_user` | globex | `gina` | A user of the other tenant. |
| `suspended_user` | acme | `sven` | A suspended user: every login is refused. |
| `service_principal` | acme | `robot` | A service principal; owns the managed calendar and has no password. |
| `service_grantee` | acme | `assistant` | A service principal that is granted the group calendar (read-write) and the managed calendar (read); works through the API and MCP. |
| `service_writer` | acme | `importer` | A service principal that is granted the managed calendar for reading and writing: the API and MCP write where DAV is capped at read. |
| `tenant_token` | acme | - | An administrator token of the tenant with every tenant scope. |
| `other_tenant_token` | globex | - | An administrator token of the other tenant. |
| `system_token` | - | - | A system token (tenant administration of the installation). |
| `anonymous` | - | - | No credential at all. |

## Calendars

| Calendar | Owner | Slug | Kind | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `personal` | `olivia` | `personal` | Personal | The personal calendar of the owner. |
| `group` | `team` | `team-calendar` | Group | The calendar of the group `team`. |
| `managed` | `robot` | `holidays` | Managed | The managed calendar of the service principal, read-only for principals on DAV. |
| `shared` | `olivia` | `projects` | User | A user calendar of the owner that is shared with several sharees. |
| `mirror` | `olivia` | `google` | Mirror | A mirror of an external calendar, read-only on every principal surface. |

## Operations

`Needs` is the effective access that the default rules require (`none` means every authenticated principal of the tenant); `Target` says whether the operation addresses a calendar or the home of its owner. The surface columns list the scope that a token needs on the API and on MCP.

| Operation | Needs | Target | DAV | API | MCP | Feed | RSVP | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read_collection` | read | calendar | yes | `calendars:read` | `mcp:read` |  |  | Read the properties of a calendar. |
| `list_objects` | read | calendar | yes | `events:read` | `mcp:read` |  |  | List or query the objects of a calendar, or its changes. |
| `read_object` | read | calendar | yes | `events:read` | `mcp:read` |  |  | Read one object. |
| `free_busy_query` | none | calendar | yes |  | `mcp:read` |  |  | Ask for the busy time of a calendar. |
| `create_object` | read_write | calendar | yes | `events:write` | `mcp:write` |  |  | Create an object. |
| `update_object` | read_write | calendar | yes | `events:write` | `mcp:write` |  |  | Replace or change an object. |
| `delete_object` | read_write | calendar | yes | `events:write` | `mcp:write` |  |  | Delete an object. |
| `batch_upsert` | read_write | calendar |  | `events:write` |  |  |  | Create or replace several objects with one request. |
| `move_object_from` | read_write | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | MOVE: the source calendar. |
| `move_object_to` | read_write | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | MOVE: the target calendar. |
| `copy_object_from` | read | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | COPY: the source calendar. |
| `copy_object_to` | read_write | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | COPY: the target calendar. |
| `respond_to_invitation` | read_write | calendar |  |  | `mcp:write` |  |  | Answer an invitation on behalf of the caller. |
| `prop_patch_binding` | read | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | Change the properties that belong to the caller's own binding (colour, order, name). |
| `update_calendar` | read_write | calendar | yes | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Change the settings that belong to the calendar for everyone. |
| `rename_calendar` | admin | calendar |  | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Rename the calendar itself. |
| `create_calendar` | owner | home | yes | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Create a calendar in the home of the owner. |
| `delete_calendar` | owner | calendar | yes | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Delete the calendar for everyone. |
| `remove_binding` | read | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | Delete a bound calendar without being its owner: the binding goes away, unless a required grant reaches the caller, which is refused. |
| `share_calendar` | admin | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | Share the calendar (CalendarServer sharing). |
| `reply_invite` | owner | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | Accept or decline a pending invitation to a shared calendar. |
| `list_grants` | admin | calendar |  | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | List the grants of a calendar. |
| `put_grant` | admin | calendar |  | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Create or replace a grant. |
| `delete_grant` | admin | calendar |  | `calendars:write` |  |  |  | Remove a grant. |
| `read_inbox` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | Read the scheduling inbox of the home. |
| `delete_inbox_item` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | Delete an item of the scheduling inbox. |
| `post_outbox` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | POST to the scheduling outbox (free-busy requests). |
| `read_notifications` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | Read the notification collection of the home. |
| `delete_notification` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | Delete a notification. |
| `read_home` | owner | home | yes |  |  |  |  | List the home of the owner of a calendar: its bindings, and their synchronization. |
| `read_principal` | none | calendar | yes |  |  |  |  | Read the principal resource of the owner of a calendar (addresses, URL of the home). |
| `read_feed` | read | calendar |  |  |  | yes |  | Render the subscription feed of a calendar. |
| `rsvp_view` | none | calendar |  |  |  |  | yes | Open an RSVP page. |
| `rsvp_answer` | none | calendar |  |  |  |  | yes | Answer on an RSVP page. |

## Token scopes

A tenant token that carries one scope is refused (`F`) for every operation that needs another one, and allowed (`A`) for the operations of its own scope on the calendars it reaches. The table shows, per operation, the scope that is needed and the answer for a token that carries only that scope, on the personal calendar and on the group calendar.

| Surface | Operation | Scope | Personal | Group | Other scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| api | `read_collection` | `calendars:read` | A | A | F |
| api | `list_objects` | `events:read` | F* | A | F |
| api | `read_object` | `events:read` | F* | A | F |
| api | `create_object` | `events:write` | F* | A | F |
| api | `update_object` | `events:write` | F* | A | F |
| api | `delete_object` | `events:write` | F* | A | F |
| api | `batch_upsert` | `events:write` | F* | A | F |
| api | `update_calendar` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `rename_calendar` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `create_calendar` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `delete_calendar` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `list_grants` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `put_grant` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| api | `delete_grant` | `calendars:write` | A | A | F |
| mcp | `read_collection` | `mcp:read` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `list_objects` | `mcp:read` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `read_object` | `mcp:read` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `free_busy_query` | `mcp:read` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `create_object` | `mcp:write` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `update_object` | `mcp:write` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `delete_object` | `mcp:write` | H* | H* | H* |
| mcp | `respond_to_invitation` | `mcp:write` | H* | H* | H* |

## Administration operations

The operations of the management API that are not about one calendar. A token needs one of the scopes of the row; principals never administer anything (a principal token is refused whatever its scopes); a tenant token administers its tenant within its scopes and sees nothing of another tenant (`H`); a system token is allowed where `system:tenants` is listed and refused everywhere else. The table shows what each actor gets for a tenant token that carries every tenant scope; the token that carries exactly one of the scopes of a row is allowed, and the tokens that carry only other scopes are refused (`F`), for every one of the 12 scopes a tenant token can carry. An operation that names an id is also asked for by the administrator of another tenant in its own tenant with the ids of the first, and answers `H`. A `+` after the operation marks one of the operations of a service that is not offered yet (see "Pending operations").

## Rules of the administration operations

How the actors are treated (`[[admin_actor]]`) and the scopes each kind of API token may carry (`[[token_scopes]]`). A token is decided by its scopes: allowed with one of the scopes of the operation, refused without.

| Actor | Rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `group_member` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `sharee_read` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `sharee_read_write` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `grantee_via_group` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `pending_sharee` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `declined_sharee` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `other_user` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `other_tenant_user` | `other_tenant` | everything of this tenant is invisible to them |
| `suspended_user` | `unauthenticated` | no credential, or the credentials of a suspended principal |
| `service_principal` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `service_grantee` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `service_writer` | `refused` | principals never administer anything, whatever their scopes |
| `tenant_token` | `by_scope` | a tenant token administers its tenant within its scopes; a system token carries `system:tenants` only |
| `other_tenant_token` | `other_tenant` | everything of this tenant is invisible to them |
| `system_token` | `by_scope` | a tenant token administers its tenant within its scopes; a system token carries `system:tenants` only |
| `anonymous` | `unauthenticated` | no credential, or the credentials of a suspended principal |

| Token | Scopes it may carry |
| --- | --- |
| tenant | `principals:read`, `principals:write`, `credentials:write`, `calendars:read`, `calendars:write`, `events:read`, `events:write`, `webhooks:manage`, `providers:manage`, `outbox:manage`, `audit:read`, `itip:inbound` |
| system | `system:tenants` |
| principal | `calendars:read`, `calendars:write`, `events:read`, `events:write`, `mcp:read`, `mcp:write`, `mcp:schedule_external` |

## Pending operations

None: every operation of the management API is offered.

## Credentials

Which surface takes which kind of credential (a credential is bound to its surface), and what a state does to a credential that its surface takes: `A` it authenticates, `R` it is refused at the door (401 on DAV, the API and MCP, the 404 of an unknown token on the pages), `-` the state does not exist for the kind. A credential that its surface does not take is refused whatever its state.

| Surface | Takes |
| --- | --- |
| dav | `app_password` |
| api | `principal_token`, `tenant_token`, `system_token` |
| mcp | `principal_token`, `tenant_token`, `system_token` |
| feed | `feed_token` |
| rsvp | `rsvp_token` |

| State | `app_password` | `principal_token` | `tenant_token` | `system_token` | `feed_token` | `rsvp_token` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `valid` | A | A | A | A | A | A |
| `wrong_secret` | R | R | R | R | R | R |
| `unknown_prefix` | R | R | R | R | R | R |
| `malformed` | R | R | R | R | R | R |
| `revoked` | R | R | R | - | R | R |
| `expired` | - | R | R | - | - | R |
| `principal_suspended` | R | R | A | A | R | - |
| `tenant_suspended` | R | R | R | - | R | - |
| `cross_login` | R | - | - | - | - | - |
| `deleted_principal` | R | R | - | - | R | - |
| `not_bearer` | - | R | R | R | - | - |

Why, where the file says:

* `revoked` / `system_token`: a system token is revoked with an operator command that the harness does not run
* `expired` / `app_password`: these kinds do not expire
* `expired` / `principal_token`: an RSVP link expires seven days after the last instance of its event; tokens carry an expiry
* `expired` / `tenant_token`: an RSVP link expires seven days after the last instance of its event; tokens carry an expiry
* `expired` / `system_token`: these kinds do not expire
* `expired` / `feed_token`: these kinds do not expire
* `expired` / `rsvp_token`: an RSVP link expires seven days after the last instance of its event; tokens carry an expiry
* `principal_suspended` / `tenant_token`: they act as no principal
* `principal_suspended` / `system_token`: they act as no principal
* `principal_suspended` / `rsvp_token`: a guest is nobody's principal
* `tenant_suspended` / `system_token`: a system token belongs to no tenant, and the harness does not suspend its own
* `tenant_suspended` / `rsvp_token`: the plan does not say what a page of a suspended tenant shows a guest
* `cross_login` / `app_password`: the username must equal the login of the owner of the password
* `cross_login` / `principal_token`: only app passwords are presented with a login
* `cross_login` / `tenant_token`: only app passwords are presented with a login
* `cross_login` / `system_token`: only app passwords are presented with a login
* `cross_login` / `feed_token`: only app passwords are presented with a login
* `cross_login` / `rsvp_token`: only app passwords are presented with a login
* `deleted_principal` / `app_password`: deleting a principal revokes its credentials at once
* `deleted_principal` / `principal_token`: deleting a principal revokes its credentials at once
* `deleted_principal` / `tenant_token`: these credentials belong to no principal
* `deleted_principal` / `system_token`: these credentials belong to no principal
* `deleted_principal` / `feed_token`: deleting a principal revokes its credentials at once
* `deleted_principal` / `rsvp_token`: these credentials belong to no principal
* `not_bearer` / `app_password`: only API tokens are presented in a header
* `not_bearer` / `principal_token`: API tokens are accepted in the Bearer header only
* `not_bearer` / `tenant_token`: API tokens are accepted in the Bearer header only
* `not_bearer` / `system_token`: API tokens are accepted in the Bearer header only
* `not_bearer` / `feed_token`: only API tokens are presented in a header
* `not_bearer` / `rsvp_token`: only API tokens are presented in a header
